summary: Misapplied promotional credit appearing as a finalized invoice line for staging usage after out-of-order usage postbacks
description:
Issue summary: Customer CurioAI reports a promotional credit (promo-CURIO-MAR) that should have been applied as a provisional credit during hourly metering appears instead as a single finalized line on the Mar 9 invoice. Impact: Customer sees higher provisional usage during the billing window, then a large late credit on the final invoice which caused accounting confusion and a temporary payment reversal. Environment: Dedicated account using reserved GPU pool, prod - us-east, batch embedding jobs and some streaming requests.

Observed behavior:
- Provisional usage UI showed expected high token counts during a scheduled batch run on 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC.
- Invoice shows a single credit line applied at invoice close for -$4,200 with description "promo-CURIO-MAR adjustment".
- Customer expected the credit to reduce hourly provisional lines throughout the day instead of an end-of-cycle lump-sum.

Steps to reproduce (customer guidance):
1) Run a batch embedding job with retry enabled and org-id rotation (CurioAI had a scripted migration during the run).
2) Observe usage postbacks arriving out of order for microbatches where org-metadata changed due to an automated mapping update.
3) Inspect provisional_metering and invoice lines in billing dashboard.

Attached logs: customer provided raw postback receipts (postbacks_2026-03-09.tar.gz) and the invoice PDF.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: Aisha (CurioAI) says finance flagged the invoice because provisional lines didn't show the promo discount applied. They submitted postback bundle and invoice PDF. Asked SRE to check postback ordering and billing team to review credit ledger entries.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Ravi Sharma): Reproduced out-of-order postbacks in the ingestion logs for account curio-prod across a 3-minute window. Noted repeated retry with updated org mapping id 'curio-prod-v2' which differs from earlier events labeled 'curio-prod'.

2026-03-11 - Billing (Sofia Alvarez): Billing ledger shows a late allocation transaction (alloc_98765) which netted promotional credits at invoice finalization instead of per-hour allocation. This appears to be due to a credit-application step that waits for final attribution signals before applying promos to provisional lines.
2026-03-11 - Maya Chen: Informed CurioAI we are investigating and will provide a manual reallocation. Asked for any runbook or scripts used during migration that changed org metadata mid-run.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Created a hotfix branch locking usage_event -> org mapping at ingestion time to prevent reattribution on retries. Coordinating a backfill to reapply the promo to provisional lines for this invoice.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Out-of-order postbacks combined with mid-run org-id reassignment caused the billing attribution service to first ingest events under one org id then later reattribute to a different org id. The credit engine currently defers applying promos until final attribution to avoid double-crediting; when attribution changed late the promo was only applied during invoice finalization as a catch-all adjustment. Evidence: ingestion logs show event IDs duplicated with two different org tags; billing ledger shows a single invoice-level adjustment entry (alloc_98765) correlated to those event IDs. Repro steps executed in staging reproduced the finalization-only credit behavior when ingest ordering changed. Additional finding: the provisional_metering UI query uses immediate attribution while the credit-applier uses the attribution table populated by the attribution-processor job; attribution-processor only reconciles ordering at hourly batch boundaries which allowed a mismatch window.
resolution_notes:
Short-term remediation: Manually reallocated the promo across hourly provisional lines for INV-2026-03-09-58821 and issued a corrected invoice PDF to CurioAI. Applied a one-time adjustment to avoid finance churn for the customer. Medium-term fix: Deployed hotfix to ingestion service to lock usage_event -> org mapping on first-seen (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-fixer/pull/145). Added a change to attribution-processor to perform near-real-time reconciliation for events with retry headers. Follow-ups: Create automated test to simulate org-id rotation mid-run, update billing runbook to include steps when org metadata is changed during active jobs, and schedule a retro with Billing and SRE to decide whether promo application logic should prefer provisional allocation in ambiguous windows.

Workaround provided to customer: We issued a corrected invoice and temporarily disabled their auto migration during active batch windows until the hotfix is validated. Customer accepted the corrected invoice and confirmed the finance team is satisfied.

Status: Hotfix deployed to prod with monitoring; backfill job applied reallocation; follow-up task created INT-99821 to add an end-to-end CI test (billing + ingestion) and another task INT-99822 for runbook updates.
notes_for_followup: 1) Ensure backfill verification metrics are recorded and shared with CurioAI. 2) Add a smoke-test to the deployment checklist to run a small batch with retry and assert promo appears in provisional UI within 5 minutes. 3) Billing to confirm whether promo-application deferral policy needs to be changed globally.
